thread:
kevin: FYA team — customer 'NimbusHealth' on Dedicated v2.1.3 reported a potential exploit path via a transitive dependency (libzorp) — CVE-2025-0421. They can reproduce locally, logs attached. We need a backport + delivery plan for Private/VPC + air-gapped installs.

maya: saw the CVE. Upstream has a patch on main. CVSS ~7.8, exploit works with default config. Looks like a library upgrade + one small API change.

tj: can we push a hotfix image quickly? Remember air-gapped sites won't accept a public registry push.

sam: for Dedicated/Private we can't docker-pull-then-restart them remotely. Path options: customer-specific image pushed to their registry, or provide signed tarball they load offline. Both need build & sign work on our side.

maya: proposal: 1) create release/2.1.x backport branch, 2) cherry-pick upstream fix, 3) run the regression matrix, 4) produce image tag r2.1.4-hotfix-cve-0421, 5) sign artifact and produce SBOM & provenance.

kevin: question: our KMS signing flow currently uses the cloud KMS/HSM endpoint. Air-gapped customers can't reach that. Do we have a supported fallback?

tj: previously we used an 'on-host signing agent' for a customer who had an HSM in their VPC. Agent signs locally using a customer-managed key, then returns signed manifest to our release system. That required an RBAC exception: engineers granted temporary release:sign rights.

maya: we should replicate that workflow. I'll draft a small RBAC change: temporarily grant release:sign to release-owners group for this hotfix. Everything will be audited. We need to ensure audit logging for signing actions goes to the customer's audit sink per their compliance.

kevin: customer requires signed artifacts and 2nd-party audit evidence. Also stated they keep artifacts for 7 years. Ops/compliance needs to confirm retention policy.

sam: build + delivery steps (high level):
```
# backport build
git checkout -b backport/cve-0421 release/2.1.x
git cherry-pick <upstream-commit>
make deps-test
make image TAG=r2.1.4-hotfix-cve-0421
# package for offline
docker save myimage:r2.1.4-hotfix-cve-0421 -o image.tar
./release/sign-image --mode=on-host --key-id=customer_kms_key --out=image.tar.sig
# produce sbom
./tools/generate-sbom image.tar > sbom.json
```

infra-bot: build job #12458 queued for backport/cve-0421. Estimated runtime 25m. Artifacts will be uploaded to internal release bucket when done.

maya: assigning validation: tj + me for integration tests (kv cache, live prefix caching, latency P95). kevin to coordinate NimbusHealth staging window. Priority: HIGH for this backport.

kevin: I'll confirm a 48-hour staging window with customer and ask for a delegated key for on-host signing. If they can't provide KMS access, fallback is: we deliver unsigned tarball + checksum and a remote support session to sign in their environment (requires signed approval from their security contact).

tj: note for release automation: include build metadata env (commit, build id, time) and SBOM in release metadata. Also add a small canary rollout plan: 10% nodes for first 6h, monitor errors and latency, then 100% after 24h if stable.

maya: I'll add SBOM generation + canary steps to the PR. Also will add an entry to the runbook (ops/playbooks/backport-hotfix) documenting the on-host signing sequence and RBAC rollback.

kevin: also double-check any audit logging endpoints. NimbusHealth requires logs forwarded to their SIEM for every signing and deploy event. We may need to set up a short-lived forwarder.

sam: curious about testing matrix: we should run: unit/regression suite, integration tests against customer config (VPC networking + custom TLS), and a perf baseline (1k seq, p95 < target). I'll prepare a checklist.

maya: checklist items added to PR. I'll open PR now: backport/cve-0421 -> release/2.1.x. Will tag @tj @sam for review. When PR is green I'll trigger build job and post the signed artifact flow. :thumbsup:

kevin: thanks. I'll create a customer Jira and link PR. Ping me if KMS/blocker shows up.
